quizzes.title: Global Initiatives: IUCN, NTCA and IBCA (MCQ)
quizzes.passage: Global Tiger Day is observed annually by IUCN, and its official theme is Coexistence in action: Scaling solutions for people and tigers. Several initiatives link to this theme. The Integrated Tiger Habitat Conservation Programme is an IUCN initiative that supports habitat restoration, anti-poaching measures and community-led coexistence. Its work reaches the regions where wild tigers live. The National Tiger Conservation Authority, which works under the environment ministry, has also launched the NTCA Eco-Tourism Initiative. The initiative is described as integrated, so related services are brought together for visitors. Conservation of big cats also extends beyond tigers. The International Big Cat Alliance is a global initiative that covers several big cat species, not only the tiger. Countries can join the International Big Cat Alliance as ratifying members. The programmes described here work at different levels, some on habitats and others through visitor services or international membership. Tigers are also the national animal of India, known as the Royal Bengal Tiger. Tiger conservation in India is supported by Project Tiger, a programme overseen by the National Tiger Conservation Authority. Tigers are the focus of the Global Tiger Day observance. Each initiative has its own scope, and each contributes to the wider goal of protecting tigers and other big cats in the wild.

questions.q: Which of the following is one of the seven big cat species covered by the International Big Cat Alliance?
questions.explanation: The seven species are Tiger, Lion, Leopard, Snow Leopard, Cheetah, Jaguar and Puma.

questions.q: In which region does the IUCN Integrated Tiger Habitat Conservation Programme operate?
questions.explanation: The programme supports habitat restoration, anti-poaching and community-led coexistence across Asia.

questions.q: In which year was the International Big Cat Alliance launched?
questions.explanation: The International Big Cat Alliance was launched in 2023.

questions.q:
Assertion (A): The International Big Cat Alliance covers seven big cat species.
Reason (R): Countries can become ratifying members of the International Big Cat Alliance.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.explanation: Both statements are true, but ratifying membership does not explain the number of species covered.

questions.q:
Match List I with List II:
I. International Big Cat Alliance   ->   A. India-led
II. NTCA Eco-Tourism Initiative   ->   B. Integrated platform for safari and accommodation bookings
III. 1st International Big Cat Alliance Summit   ->   C. Postponed
IV. Integrated Tiger Habitat Conservation Programme   ->   D. IUCN initiative
questions.explanation: The alliance is India-led, the NTCA initiative is an integrated booking platform, the summit is marked postponed, and the habitat programme is an IUCN initiative.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
I. The IUCN Integrated Tiger Habitat Conservation Programme covers habitat restoration and anti-poaching measures.
II. The NTCA Eco-Tourism Initiative is a platform for safari and accommodation bookings.
III. The International Big Cat Alliance covers eight big cat species.
Which of the above statements is/are correct?
questions.explanation: Statement III is wrong because the alliance covers seven big cat species.

questions.q:
How many of the following statements are correct?
I. Global Tiger Day is observed annually by IUCN.
II. The International Big Cat Alliance was launched in 2010.
III. The NTCA Eco-Tourism Initiative was launched by the National Tiger Conservation Authority.
questions.explanation: Statements I and III are correct, while II is wrong because the alliance was launched in 2023.

quizzes.title: Global Initiatives: IUCN, NTCA and IBCA (TITA)
quizzes.passage: Protecting tigers requires work on habitats, on poaching and on the relationship between wild animals and people. The Integrated Tiger Habitat Conservation Programme is an initiative of the International Union for Conservation of Nature, known as IUCN. It focuses on restoring habitats, reducing poaching and encouraging communities to coexist with tigers. A separate effort is the NTCA Eco-Tourism Initiative, launched by the National Tiger Conservation Authority. The initiative is described as an integrated platform that offers authentic safari and accommodation bookings for visitors. Conservation of big cats also extends beyond tigers. The International Big Cat Alliance is a global initiative, and it covers several big cat species rather than only the tiger. Countries can join the alliance as ratifying members. Tiger Range Countries have also committed to a goal called TX2, which aimed to double the global wild tiger population by 2022. Global Tiger Day is observed each year by IUCN. Each of these efforts works at a different level, from habitats on the ground to international membership. Tigers are one of the big cat species, alongside lions, leopards and jaguars. The NTCA initiative and the IUCN programme cover different parts of the effort, one focused on visitors and the other on habitats and communities.

questions.q: How many big cat species does the International Big Cat Alliance cover? (number)
questions.explanation: The alliance covers seven big cat species, including the tiger.

questions.q: In which year was the International Big Cat Alliance launched? (year)
questions.explanation: The International Big Cat Alliance was launched in 2023.

questions.q: Which region does the IUCN Integrated Tiger Habitat Conservation Programme cover? (name of region)
questions.explanation: The programme works across Asia on habitat restoration, anti-poaching and coexistence.

questions.q: In which city was the 1st International Big Cat Alliance Summit scheduled? (city)
questions.explanation: The summit was scheduled in New Delhi and is marked postponed.

questions.q: In which month was the 1st International Big Cat Alliance Summit scheduled? (month)
questions.explanation: The summit was scheduled for June 2026.

questions.q: How many initial ratifying members did the International Big Cat Alliance have? (number)
questions.explanation: The initial five ratifying members were India, Nicaragua, Eswatini, Somalia and Liberia.

questions.q: Which country leads the International Big Cat Alliance? (country)
questions.explanation: The alliance is an India-led global initiative.

quizzes.title: Indian Institutions and Milestones (MCQ)
quizzes.passage: India's wildlife protection rests on a set of statutory bodies, policies and programmes. The National Board for Wild Life is one of the central institutions, and its role is to promote the conservation and development of wildlife and forests. Its scope covers both animals and the forest areas they live in. Project Tiger is a programme set up to support the preservation of tigers in India. It works through tiger reserves, which are notified by state governments. Monitoring of these reserves is also an important part of the work, and one system used in this area carries the name M-STrIPES. Tiger population is estimated through a census cycle, repeated at fixed intervals. More than one institution takes part in the census. Project Tiger is overseen by the National Tiger Conservation Authority, which is a statutory body under the Wild Life Protection Act. Tiger reserves are specially designated protected areas under Project Tiger. Changes to the boundaries of a tiger reserve require a recommendation from the authority and approval of the National Board for Wild Life. Legal and administrative steps have shaped the system over time. The Wild Life Protection Act was amended in 2006. The authority works under the environment ministry and is chaired by the minister in charge of that ministry.

questions.q: What does M-STrIPES stand for?
options: Multi-State Tiger Reporting and Information Program for Ecological Safety
Management System for Tiger Rehabilitation in Protected Ecosystems
Mapping System for Tiger Range and Indigenous Protection
Monitoring System for Tigers - Intensive Protection and Ecological Status
questions.explanation: M-STrIPES stands for Monitoring System for Tigers - Intensive Protection and Ecological Status.

questions.q: How many years does one tiger census cycle last?
questions.explanation: The tiger census estimates the population through a 4-year census cycle.

questions.q: Which trade was banned in India in 1969?
options: Export of all wild cat skins
questions.explanation: In 1969 the export of all wild cat skins was banned.

questions.q:
Assertion (A): The National Board for Wild Life is a statutory board.
Reason (R): It is constituted under the Wild Life Protection Act, 1972.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.explanation: The board's statutory status comes from the Act under which it is constituted.

questions.q:
Match List I with List II:
I. 1969   ->   A. Ban on export of wild cat skins
II. 1972   ->   B. Wild Life Protection Act enacted
III. 2010   ->   C. Software-based monitoring system for tiger reserves (M-STrIPES)
IV. 2023   ->   D. International Big Cat Alliance launched
questions.explanation: The 1969 ban, the 1972 Act, the 2010 M-STrIPES system and the 2023 alliance launch are each matched to their own entry.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
I. The Wild Life Protection Act was enacted in 1972.
II. The tiger census is conducted every three years.
III. M-STrIPES was introduced in 2010.
Which of the above statements is/are correct?
questions.explanation: Statement II is wrong because the census runs on a 4-year cycle.

questions.q:
How many of the following statements are correct?
I. The export ban on wild cat skins was imposed in 1969.
II. The 2006 amendment to the wildlife law resulted in the creation of the Wildlife Crime Control Bureau.
III. The National Tiger Conservation Authority was established in 2010.
questions.explanation: Statements I and II are correct, while III is wrong because the authority predates 2010.

quizzes.title: Indian Institutions and Milestones (TITA)
quizzes.passage: Wildlife protection in India rests on a set of institutions, each with a defined role. Several bodies share this work. The National Board for Wild Life is a statutory board, and its responsibilities include the promotion of conservation and development of wildlife and forests. Its legal basis lies in the Wild Life Protection Act. Project Tiger is a programme set up to support the preservation of tigers. Its tiger reserves are notified by state governments, and any change to their boundaries needs a recommendation from the National Tiger Conservation Authority and approval from the board. The authority is itself a statutory body, and it oversees Project Tiger. Population monitoring is a continuing task. The tiger population is estimated through a census cycle that repeats at fixed intervals, and more than one institution takes part in the census. One software-based system used in this area carries the name M-STrIPES, which is a monitoring system for tiger reserves. Legal and administrative steps have shaped the system over time. Changes to the wildlife law have also led to new bodies. The authority works under the environment ministry and is chaired by the minister in charge of that ministry. Tiger reserves are specially designated protected areas under Project Tiger.

questions.q: How many years does one tiger census cycle last? (number)
questions.explanation: The tiger population is estimated through a 4-year census cycle.

questions.q: In which year was the Wild Life Protection Act enacted? (year)
questions.explanation: The Wild Life Protection Act was enacted in 1972.

questions.q: What is the acronym of the bureau set up as a result of the 2006 amendment to the wildlife law? (acronym)
questions.explanation: The 2006 amendment resulted in the Wildlife Crime Control Bureau, abbreviated WCCB.

questions.q: In which year was the M-STrIPES monitoring system introduced? (year)
questions.explanation: M-STrIPES was introduced in 2010 as a software-based monitoring system.

questions.q: In which year was the export ban on all wild cat skins imposed? (year)
questions.explanation: India banned the export of all wild cat skins in 1969.

questions.q: What is the acronym of the ministry under which the National Tiger Conservation Authority works? (acronym)
questions.explanation: The authority works under the Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change, abbreviated MoEFCC.

questions.q: Which institute, besides the NTCA, takes part in India's tiger census? (acronym)
questions.explanation: The tiger census is conducted by the NTCA and the Wildlife Institute of India, abbreviated WII.
